# FINAL IVX PRODUCTION COMPLETION ORDER

## EXECUTE THE WORK — DO NOT ONLY RETURN A REPORT

The previous narrative report is not accepted as proof of production completion.

Do not return another generic “PASS,” “completed,” “production-ready,” or “verified” statement without direct, independently checkable evidence.

You are authorized to diagnose, repair, test, build, and prepare deployment. Production deployment still requires explicit owner approval immediately before the production deployment action.

---

# 1. DEPLOYMENT AND SOURCE-OF-TRUTH PROOF

Identify and verify the actual source controlling production.

Provide:

* Active GitHub repository URL.
* Active production branch.
* GitHub HEAD commit SHA.
* Exact commit SHA currently running in production.
* Confirmation that GitHub HEAD and the live production commit match.
* Render service name.
* Render deployment ID.
* Render deployment status.
* Render deployment timestamp.
* EAS Android production build ID.
* EAS build profile used.
* Android application ID/package name.
* App version.
* Android versionCode.
* Final directly installable APK or valid APK download link.
* Production web URL.
* Production chat URL.
* Production API URL.

Call the production `/health` endpoint and return the unmodified result showing:

* HTTP status code.
* Commit SHA.
* Build version.
* Environment.
* Boot time.
* Service name.
* Deployment identifier, when available.
* Database connectivity status.
* Supabase connectivity status.

Required acceptance condition:

```text
GITHUB_HEAD_SHA == LIVE_PRODUCTION_SHA
```

If the commits do not match, status must be `BLOCKED` or `PARTIAL`. Do not claim production completion.

---

# 2. OWNER AUTHENTICATION — COMPLETE CROSS-PLATFORM TEST

Test the real production owner account on:

* Android production APK.
* iOS production build or approved iOS test build.
* Production web application.

Test every workflow:

1. Open the logged-out application.
2. Enter the owner email manually.
3. Enter the owner password manually.
4. Complete login.
5. Confirm the authenticated owner identity.
6. Confirm the correct owner role is loaded.
7. Open Owner Dashboard.
8. Open Admin Hub.
9. Open Settings.
10. Open Variables.
11. Logout.
12. Login again manually.
13. Fully close the application.
14. Restart the application.
15. Verify valid session persistence.
16. Enter an invalid password and confirm rejection.
17. Test a non-owner account and confirm owner-route rejection.
18. Confirm no automatic login occurs after an intentional logout.
19. Confirm expired or invalid sessions return to login safely.
20. Confirm no infinite loader or blank screen occurs.

For every platform provide:

* Device or browser.
* Operating system/version.
* App/build version.
* UTC and local test timestamp.
* Route tested.
* Expected result.
* Actual result.
* HTTP status.
* Relevant logs.
* Screenshot or video evidence.
* Trace ID or request ID when available.

Owner authentication is not verified unless Android, iOS, and web all pass.

---

# 3. SUPABASE PRODUCTION DATA RECOVERY AND RECONCILIATION

Audit the real production Supabase project.

Back up all affected tables before modifying or deleting any record.

Audit and reconcile:

* Members.
* Investors.
* Buyers.
* Properties.
* Deals.
* Investment cards.
* Reels.
* Conversations.
* Messages.
* Media.
* Documents.
* Revenue.
* Transactions.
* Landing submissions.
* Notifications.
* User profiles.
* Roles and permissions.

For every dataset provide:

| Dataset | Database total | Android UI total | iOS UI total | Web UI total | Duplicates | Invalid rows | Status |
| ------- | -------------: | ---------------: | -----------: | -----------: | ---------: | -----------: | ------ |

Required work:

* Identify the source table used by each UI module.
* Confirm the API query used by each platform.
* Confirm owner access policies.
* Confirm Supabase RLS policies.
* Confirm pagination is not hiding records.
* Confirm filters are not excluding legitimate records.
* Confirm deleted or archived records are handled correctly.
* Confirm Android, iOS, and web display the same production records.
* Identify duplicate records using stable keys.
* Identify fake, seeded, demo, or test records.
* Identify orphaned media and documents.
* Identify broken foreign-key relationships.

Do not delete fake or duplicate production data without:

1. Creating a backup.
2. Producing a deletion candidate list.
3. Receiving explicit owner approval.

---

# 4. CORE MODULE END-TO-END VERIFICATION

Test every production route and its primary actions.

Modules:

* Landing page.
* Registration.
* Email verification.
* Phone verification.
* Members.
* Investors.
* Buyers.
* Properties.
* Deals.
* Investment cards.
* Reels.
* IVX IA chat.
* Notifications.
* Media uploads.
* Image uploads.
* Video uploads.
* Documents.
* Revenue.
* Transactions.
* Analytics.
* Owner Dashboard.
* Admin Hub.
* Settings.
* Variables.
* Admin editing.
* Admin deletion.
* Search.
* Filtering.
* Pagination.
* Logout.

For each module provide:

| Module | Route | Action | Expected | Actual | HTTP/API status | Database effect | Evidence | Status |
| ------ | ----- | ------ | -------- | ------ | --------------- | --------------- | -------- | ------ |

Every action must include:

* Exact route tested.
* Exact UI action.
* Exact API endpoint.
* HTTP method.
* HTTP response code.
* Request ID or trace ID.
* Database table affected.
* Record ID created, updated, or deleted.
* Screenshot or video.
* Exact error message if unsuccessful.
* File and function responsible if a code defect is identified.

Do not mark a module verified because it merely opens. Its primary read, create, update, and permitted delete workflows must be tested.

---

# 5. IVX IA SENIOR-DEVELOPER EXECUTION PROOF

IVX IA must demonstrate real repository and deployment capabilities.

It must prove it can:

1. Access the active repository.
2. Read repository files.
3. Search for routes, components, services, hooks, and functions.
4. Identify the file responsible for a reported defect.
5. Read runtime and deployment logs.
6. Diagnose the root cause.
7. Modify the correct source file.
8. Run formatting.
9. Run lint.
10. Run TypeScript type checking.
11. Run unit tests.
12. Run integration tests.
13. Run API tests.
14. Run the production build.
15. Produce a Git diff.
16. Create a Git commit.
17. Push the commit to the approved branch.
18. Return the commit SHA.
19. Request owner approval before production deployment.
20. Deploy only after explicit authorization.
21. Return deployment ID and deployment logs.
22. Verify the live route after deployment.
23. Return the final live `/health` result.

Required evidence:

* Repository path.
* Files inspected.
* Files changed.
* Functions changed.
* Git diff summary.
* Test commands.
* Full command results.
* Commit SHA.
* Branch.
* Deployment ID.
* Live verification.

A text explanation without repository actions, file changes, tests, commit creation, and deployment evidence is not senior-developer execution.

---

# 6. ANDROID PRODUCTION APK QA

Test the final Android production APK independently from Expo Go.

Required tests:

* APK downloads successfully.
* APK installs directly.
* Package signature is valid.
* Application opens without Expo Go.
* No Metro server is required.
* No `exp://` URL is required.
* No dependency on `169.254.x.x`.
* Owner login succeeds.
* Logout succeeds.
* Session persistence works.
* Members load.
* Investors load.
* Buyers load.
* Properties load.
* Investment cards open.
* Reels load and play.
* Reels do not crash.
* Chat room opens.
* Keyboard opens.
* Keyboard does not cover the composer.
* Messages send.
* Messages persist after restart.
* Message order remains stable.
* Duplicate messages do not appear.
* Images upload.
* Videos upload.
* Documents upload.
* Notifications work.
* No white top banner.
* No jumping landing page.
* No jumping posts.
* No infinite loaders.
* No blank routes.
* No missing routes.
* No developer-only screens.
* No Rork branding, SDK, banner, or unauthorized control remains.

Provide:

* Device model.
* Android version.
* APK filename.
* File size.
* SHA-256 checksum.
* Package name.
* App version.
* versionCode.
* Installation timestamp.
* Launch timestamp.
* Screenshots or recording.
* Crash logs, if any.

---

# 7. IOS PRODUCTION SMOKE TEST

Test the equivalent production iOS build or authorized TestFlight build.

Verify:

* Installation.
* Launch.
* Owner login.
* Logout.
* Session persistence.
* Members.
* Investors.
* Properties.
* Investment cards.
* Reels.
* Chat.
* Keyboard.
* Message persistence.
* Image upload.
* Video upload.
* Documents.
* Notifications.
* No missing route.
* No infinite loader.
* No crash.

Provide the iOS build number, version, device, OS version, timestamps, screenshots, and logs.

---

# 8. WEB PRODUCTION SMOKE TEST

Test the live production web URLs in current desktop and mobile browsers.

Verify:

* Landing page loads.
* Registration works.
* Owner login works.
* Owner Dashboard loads.
* Admin Hub loads.
* Members load.
* Investors load.
* Buyers load.
* Properties load.
* Investment cards load.
* Reels load.
* Chat works.
* Keyboard and composer work on mobile browser.
* Media uploads work.
* Documents work.
* Revenue and transactions load.
* Analytics loads.
* Logout works.
* Unauthorized routes are protected.
* No console-critical errors.
* No failed critical network requests.
* No page jumping.
* No white banner.
* No infinite loader.

---

# 9. COMPLETE FINAL TEST GATE

Run and report:

* Formatting checks.
* Lint.
* TypeScript type checking.
* Unit tests.
* Integration tests.
* API tests.
* Authentication tests.
* Authorization tests.
* Supabase RLS tests.
* Database integrity tests.
* Data reconciliation tests.
* End-to-end tests.
* Android production smoke test.
* iOS smoke test.
* Web production smoke test.
* Upload tests.
* Chat persistence tests.
* Reels playback tests.
* Owner-route protection tests.
* Health endpoint tests.

Return:

| Test suite | Passed | Failed | Skipped | Duration | Evidence |
| ---------- | -----: | -----: | ------: | -------: | -------- |

Critical workflows that must have zero failures:

* Production application launch.
* Owner login.
* Owner authorization.
* Members loading.
* Investors loading.
* Properties loading.
* Investment cards.
* Reels playback.
* IVX IA chat.
* Message persistence.
* Production API health.
* Production database connectivity.
* Android APK installation.

---

# 10. FINAL DELIVERABLE PACKAGE

Return one final evidence package containing:

## Source and deployment

* GitHub repository.
* GitHub branch.
* GitHub HEAD SHA.
* Live production SHA.
* Render service.
* Render deploy ID.
* Render status.
* EAS Android build ID.
* iOS build ID/build number.
* APK filename.
* APK download link.
* APK SHA-256.
* Production URLs.
* `/health` output.

## Testing

* Total tests passed.
* Total tests failed.
* Total tests skipped.
* Android result.
* iOS result.
* Web result.
* API result.
* Authentication result.
* Database result.

## Production data

* Database totals.
* Android UI totals.
* iOS UI totals.
* Web UI totals.
* Duplicate totals.
* Fake/test record totals.
* Unresolved reconciliation differences.

## Evidence

* Screenshots.
* Videos.
* Logs.
* Trace IDs.
* API responses.
* Database evidence.
* Build logs.
* Deployment logs.

## Operational safety

* Known remaining issues.
* Severity of each issue.
* Exact affected file.
* Exact affected function.
* Exact service.
* Exact route.
* Exact error code.
* Required correction.
* Rollback commit.
* Rollback deployment procedure.
* Database rollback procedure.

---

# FINAL STATUS RULE

Only use:

```text
VERIFIED
```

when all of the following have direct evidence:

* Live production application tested.
* Production API tested.
* Production Supabase database tested.
* GitHub HEAD matches the live commit.
* Android production APK installed and tested.
* Owner authentication passed on Android, iOS, and web.
* Critical production data displays correctly.
* Core modules passed.
* Critical test failures equal zero.

Use:

```text
PARTIAL
```

when some work is complete but one or more required validations remain.

Use:

```text
BLOCKED
```

when execution cannot continue because of a specific technical failure.

For `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED`, report:

* Exact repository.
* Exact branch.
* Exact file.
* Exact function.
* Exact service.
* Exact route.
* Exact command.
* Exact error message.
* HTTP or platform error code.
* Correction required.
* Whether owner action is actually required.

Do not request credentials merely because an integration failed.

Credentials and secrets must be assumed to already exist in approved secret storage. First verify:

* Secret name.
* Runtime binding.
* Deployment environment.
* Service access.
* Token scope.
* API response.
* Exact 401 or 403 response.

Only request credential replacement when direct evidence proves the credential is missing, expired, revoked, deleted, invalid, or unauthorized.

Do not invent evidence.

Do not fabricate screenshots, deployment IDs, commits, build IDs, database totals, logs, API responses, or test results.

Do not call the application verified based on narrative analysis.

Execute, test, repair, build, and return direct production evidence.
